objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with sudden loss of vision in one eye.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I’m a 60-year-old woman, and about 30 minutes ago while I was watching TV I suddenly lost vision in my right eye. It was painless, and I haven’t noticed any other symptoms.
Is your vision still absent in the right eye, or has it returned to normal since it began 30 minutes ago?
Yes, the vision in my right eye is still absent right now—it hasn’t returned to normal since it started about 30 minutes ago.
Do you have any headache, tenderness over your temples, or jaw pain when chewing food?
“No, I don’t have any headache, no tenderness over my temples, and no jaw pain when I chew.”
Did you notice any flashes of light, new floaters, or a curtain-like shadow coming across your vision right before or during this episode?
“No, I didn’t notice any flashes of light or new floaters, and I haven’t seen a curtain-like shadow across my vision.”
Do you have any history of high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, smoking, heart disease, or an irregular heartbeat such as atrial fibrillation?
Yes—I have high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes, and I also have coronary artery disease. I don’t smoke, and I’m not sure about any irregular heartbeat.
Can you see any light at all with your right eye, or is the vision completely black?
“My right eye is completely black—no light at all. I can only see normally with my left eye.”
Do you have any pain in or around your right eye, especially when you move the eye?
“No pain around my right eye, and I haven’t noticed any pain when I move it. It’s just that my right eye vision is completely absent and hasn’t come back since it started.”
Have you ever had previous episodes where your vision in either eye went black or dim for a few minutes and then returned to normal?
“No, I haven’t had any prior episodes like that where my vision went black or dim and then returned to normal.”
When you shine a bright light into your right eye (or cover your left eye and expose the right eye to light), does the pupil get smaller, or does it stay large and not react?

“My right pupil doesn’t seem to shrink when the light is shined into my right eye—it looks like it stays about the same size. My vision there is completely absent, while my left eye still responds to light normally.”
[DDX] Central retinal artery occlusion, Ischemic optic neuropathy (anterior), Giant cell arteritis, Central retinal vein occlusion, Retinal detachment
